sentences.text:
criminal proceedings initiated again them in C.C.No.3029/2022 (Crime No.129/2022) for the offences punishable under Sections 323, 498-A, 504, 506 R/w 149 of Indian Penal Code and Section 4 of the Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961.
2.
Petitioners have contended that the criminal proceeding are initiated against them on the basis of false complaint filed by respondent No.2.
There are no material to connect petitioners with the alleged crime.
Even according to the complasint averments respondent No.2 stayed only for six months in the matrimonial home after the marriage.
Therefore question of petitioners planning to kill her on 16.09.2018 does not arise.
On 03.03.2018 and 12.03.2018, petitioner No.1 has issued legal notice to respondent No.1.
On 16.03.2018 respondent No.2 has sent replied to the legal notice.
Such being the case on 16.09.2018 question of complainant over hearing petitioners planning to eliminate her would not arise.
In fact there are no such allegations regarding petitioners subjecting respondent No.2 to cruelty and other allegations in the reply notice.
Since 2012 petitioner No.1 and respondent No.2 have not live together.

After failure of conciliation proceedings and initiation of matrimonial proceedings, respondent No.2 has chosen to file the complaint as a measure of arm twisting and prays to allow the petition and quash the criminal proceedings initiated against the petitioners.

3. In support of his arguments learned counsel for the petitioners has relied upon the following decisions:
i) Kahkashan Kausar @ Sonam & Ors. Vs. State of Bihar & Ors.1 (Kahkashan Kausar)
ii) Mr. Mohammed Shameer S/o Mohammed Muneer and others vs. State of Karnataka and another.2 (Mr. Mohammed Shameer) Crl.A.No.195/2022 dated 08.02.2022 Crl.P.No.521/2022 dated 10.05.2022 4.

sentences.text: Learned counsel representing respondent No.2 submits that petitioner No.1 has contacted second marriage and a son is born through the second marriage.
Learned High Court Government Pleader representing the respondent No.1/State submitted that after conducting detailed investigation charge sheet is filed against the petitioners.
The same is required to be proved at trial and prays to dismiss the petition.

5. Heard arguments and perused the records.
6.
As evident from the material placed on record and marriage of petitioner No.1 and respondent No.2 took place on 20.02.2011.
Respondent No.2 has chosen to file complaint on 03.02.2022.

In the complaint, she has alleged that right from the inception, petitioners who are greedy, harassed and ill-treated her to bring dowry of Rs.5,00,000/- and in this regard her father, mother, uncle and one Neurupadigouda advised them.

She has alleged that on 16.09.2018 at 11 p.m. while she was sleeping,
petitioners were conferencing among themselves to kill respondent No.2 and when they realized that she is listening to them, they assaulted and abused her and forced her to write a death note .
Immediately she called her father and informed him.
Her father came and took her to his house.
She waited for petitioner No.1 to come and take her and ultimately has filed the complaint.

sentences.text: On the other hand to show that after the marriage respondent No.2 stayed for a very short period with him, Petitioner No.1 has produced copy of the legal notice dated 03.03.2018 sent by him to respondent No.2.
When she refused to take the notice he has sent one more notice dated 12.03.2018.

In the said notices petitioner No.1 has alleged that after the marriage only for a period of six month they lived together peacefully, after which respondent No.2 started picking up quarrel on petty matters and leaving matrimonial home frequently.
Though petitioner No.1 brought her back many times, ultimately since six months she is living in her parental home and refused to return, despite petitioner No.1 went to bring her back.

In the notice he has called upon respondent No.2 to give consent for divorce within a period of seven days from the date of service of notice, failing which he would be constrained to initiate divorce proceedings.
8. To notice dated 12.03.2018 respondent No.2 has sent reply alleging that on the ill-advise of his parents petitioner No.1 has ousted respondent No.2 from the matrimonial home about 5-6 months back.
During her stay petitioner No.1 was abusing her, neglected and tortured her.
She was not provided with food and medicine.
He is doing this to take a second wife in order to get dowry.
9. In this notice, there are no allegations that petitioners demanded dowry in a sum of Rs.5,00,000/- and for the said reasons harassed and ill-treated her.

There is also no allegations of petitioners conspiring to kill her on the night of 16.09.2018 at 11 p.m. and that they assaulted her and forced to writ a death note and on the next day her father came and took her back.

Though respondent No.2 has made a serious allegation of threat to her life on 16.09.2018, she has chosen to file complaint on 03.05.2022, after lapse of nearly four years, that too, after receipt of legal notice.

Though the learned counsel for respondent No.2 submitted that petitioner No.1 has contracted a second marriage and a son is born through the said wedlock, neither in the reply notice nor in the complaint she has made such allegations.

From the manner in which respondent No.2 has chosen to file belated complaint after receipt of legal notice goes to show that as an after thought and as an arm twisting, she has chosen to file a false complaint making serious allegations against the petitioners.

10. In the light of the above discussions and the decisions relied upon by the petitioners I am of the considered opinion that continuation of the criminal proceedings would amount to abuse of the process of the Court and as such liable to be quashed and accordingly, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
The petition is allowed.

The impugned proceedings in C.C.No.3029/2022 (Crime No.129/2022) for the offences punishable under Sections 323, 498-A, 504, 506 R/w 149 of Indian Penal Code and Section 4 of the Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961 pending on the file of Principal Civil Judge and JMFC, Gangavati, insofar as petitioners are concerned, is hereby quashed.

In view of disposal of the matter, pending interlocutory applications, if any, do not survive for consideration and are disposed of accordingly.
